FANI WILLIS.name: Fani Willis
FANI WILLIS.background: Fani Willis earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Howard University (1993) and a J.D. from Emory Law School (1996). She was a prosecutor in the Fulton County District Attorney's office from 2001 to 2018 (deputy DA), then ran a private practice (from 2018) and was chief magistrate judge of the City of South Fulton (from 2019). She ran for an open Atlanta Circuit Superior Court seat in 2018 and lost the July runoff to Kevin Farmer (44.7%). In 2020 she unseated incumbent DA Paul Howard Jr. in a Democratic primary runoff (71.7%) and was unopposed in November. She took office Jan. 1, 2021 as Fulton's first Black woman DA. She was re-elected in 2024, beating Christian Wise Smith in the primary (87.0%) and Republican Courtney Kramer in November (68.1%).
FANI WILLIS.ideology: Some progressives and defense attorneys say Willis overuses gang and racketeering laws (AP, 2024). Willis called her 2024 Republican opponent 'a right-wing politician.'
FANI WILLIS.record: In February 2021 Willis opened an investigation into efforts to overturn Georgia's 2020 presidential result. In August 2023 her office obtained a racketeering indictment of Donald Trump and 18 others (41 counts); four defendants pleaded guilty under deals, and Trump pleaded not guilty. In January 2024 defendant Michael Roman moved to disqualify her over her relationship with special prosecutor Nathan Wade. On March 15, 2024, Judge Scott McAfee ruled that she could stay only if Wade withdrew, and Wade resigned that day; a judge called the relationship a 'tremendous lapse in judgment.' The Georgia Court of Appeals later removed her from the case. Prosecutor Peter Skandalakis took it over, and the remaining charges were dismissed on Nov. 26, 2025.
